descripcion: At B2 hedging and the passive are learned separately and start to appear together: a hedge softens a claim, the passive removes an unnecessary actor. The full three-layer academic stack with impersonal reporting verbs (C1) isn't the target yet — using one or two of these tools together is enough.

cuadroReferencia.titulo: Combining a hedge with the passive
filas: The results were published last year.
It may not have been reported accurately.

ejemplos.texto: This may not be entirely accurate.
The results were published without much detail.
It might not have been checked properly.

notas: A hedge (may, might, could) softens a claim without changing its basic meaning.
The passive removes the actor when it isn't important or isn't known — the report was delayed, not someone delayed the report.
Combining a hedge with the passive is common in careful, professional English but shouldn't be used on every sentence.

es.en: Spanish hedges mainly with the conditional and uses the passive less as a device for distance, preferring the impersonal se. Spanish speakers tend to under-hedge in formal English, because in Spanish one layer is usually enough.
es.es: El español atenúa principalmente con el condicional y usa menos el pasivo como recurso de distanciamiento, prefiriendo el «se» impersonal. Los hispanohablantes tienden a atenuar demasiado poco en inglés formal, porque en español una sola capa suele bastar.

de.en: German academic prose uses the passive and man freely, so removing the actor is familiar. The hedging layer is less graded (wohl, dürfte, vermutlich), and man is often calqued as one, which sounds stiff in most English texts.
de.de: Deutsche wissenschaftliche Texte verwenden Passiv und «man» sehr frei, daher ist das Weglassen des Handelnden vertraut. Die Abstufung von Abschwächungen ist weniger fein («wohl, dürfte, vermutlich»), und «man» wird oft als «one» übertragen, was in den meisten englischen Texten steif klingt.

it.en: Italian hedges with the condizionale and the si impersonale (si ritiene che, sembrerebbe), which match it is thought that and it would appear. The risk is stacking conditionals where English uses one lexical hedge (may, likely) plus a passive.
it.it: L'italiano attenua con il condizionale e il «si» impersonale («si ritiene che», «sembrerebbe»), che corrispondono a «it is thought that» e «it would appear». Il rischio è accumulare condizionali dove l'inglese usa un solo hedge lessicale («may», «likely») più un passivo.

fr.en: French hedges with the conditionnel and on (on pourrait penser que, il semblerait que). The calque one could think that sounds stilted; it could be argued that or it would appear that is the natural English equivalent.
fr.fr: Le français atténue avec le conditionnel et «on» («on pourrait penser que», «il semblerait que»). Le calque «one could think that» sonne guindé ; les équivalents naturels sont «it could be argued that» ou «it would appear that».

pt.en: Portuguese hedges with the se impersonal (considera-se que) and, in European Portuguese, with the future (poderá indicar). The calque will indicate is far too certain; may indicate or appears to indicate is the English equivalent.
pt.pt: O português atenua com o «se» impessoal («considera-se que») e, no português europeu, com o futuro («poderá indicar»). O calque «will indicate» é certo demais; os equivalentes ingleses são «may indicate» ou «appears to indicate».

errores: Using the passive without any hedge on a claim that is actually uncertain.
Overusing hedges on facts that are actually certain.
Forgetting the participle when combining a modal with the passive: may not checked instead of may not have been checked.

traducciones.fr: Il se peut que ça n’ait pas été…

redemittel.funcion: impersonal report of a common claim

traducciones.fr: La décision a été prise de…
traducciones.it: È stata presa la decisione di…

traducciones.fr: Je n'en suis pas certain, mais…

autochequeo: Is at least one hedge used on an uncertain claim?
Is the passive used where the actor genuinely doesn't matter?
Is the participle correct when a hedge and the passive are combined?
Have I avoided hedging a fact that's actually certain?
Does at least one sentence combine both tools?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on hedging and the passive, together and separately. Check the participle form when they're combined and whether the hedge fits the actual certainty of the claim. Do not rewrite the text.

es: «*se supone que*» rendered as *It supposes that* instead of *It is assumed that*.
de: *Es ist anzunehmen* rendered as *It is to assume that* instead of *It can be assumed that*.
it: «*si suppone che*» rendered as *It supposes that* instead of *It is assumed that*.
fr: «*on suppose que*» rendered as *One supposes that* instead of *It is assumed that*.
pt: «*supõe-se que*» rendered as *It supposes that* instead of *It is assumed that*.
